close_reason: Already-improved: the sentinel-string pattern has been replaced by a typed RequiredPermissions enum that's fail-closed by construction. No further action needed.
description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/permissions.rs:43-122 (UNKNOWN_OP_SENTINEL + match arm).

SpacePatchOp is #[non_exhaustive] upstream. A future-added variant cannot be matched at compile time from this crate. The match's wildcard arm returns &[UNKNOWN_OP_SENTINEL], where UNKNOWN_OP_SENTINEL = '__unknown_space_patch_op__' — a string no realistic caller will ever hold.

This is fail-closed: a backend evaluating the required-permission set against the caller's effective permissions will reject the op (because the caller doesn't hold the sentinel). The doc-comment is explicit: 'Backends that observe this sentinel MUST reject the op.'

A future contributor might propose:
- 'Return empty slice for unknown variants — let the backend's other checks fire.' Bad — empty required set means 'no permission required', which permits the op. Fail open, not closed.
- 'Panic on unknown variants — they shouldn't exist.' Bad — kit consumers may legitimately receive ops they haven't recompiled against (jmap-chat-types upgrade across major versions).
- 'Use an Err variant on a Result return type.' Possible, but invasively reshapes the helper's signature and forces every caller into match. The sentinel is a workable kludge given the non_exhaustive constraint.

The current shape — fail closed with an unmistakable sentinel string — is the right call. Preserve.

Note: this same pattern is repeated in MemoryBackend's apply_space_patch_impl wildcard arm (memory.rs:1198-1203, stub_description fn). They reinforce each other; both should change together if the pattern ever evolves.
title: permissions::required_permissions_for_op fails closed with sentinel string for unknown SpacePatchOp variants
